title: IHL Group homepage: retail technology research and advisory landing page
answer: IHL Group's homepage is a retail technology research and advisory landing page. Its most useful point for AI in retail is that a 2026 study of 96 specialty retail brands, with Chain Store Age, found inventory data accuracy, not AI budget size, separates winners from laggards. The page also reports that most retail AI budgets fund the wrong layer first, and that inventory distortion is down to $1.7 trillion while empty shelves still cost $690.9 billion.

sections.body: IHL Group publishes this page. It is the company's retail technology research and advisory landing page, harvested on 29 September 2026. It presents IHL Group's services and a dated feed of article summaries about retail technology, AI, inventory, media, hiring and customer service. The page is commercial in purpose and functions mainly as an index of recent items rather than a full report.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page leads with IHL Group's description of itself as a provider of detailed research and advisory services for retail technology. Its dated items begin on 10 September 2026 with an OnDemand study, SPEND SMART: How Smart Technology and AI Are Closing the Inventory Visibility Gap in Specialty Stores by Greg Buzek. IHL Group's 2026 study of 96 specialty retail brands, in cooperation with Chain Store Age, finds inventory data accuracy, not AI budget size, separates specialty retail winners from laggards. On 26 August 2026 IHL Group says most retail AI budgets fund the wrong layer first and points to what is stalling AI pilots before they reach the store floor in 2026. On 6 August 2026 it says inventory distortion is down to $1.7 trillion, but empty shelves still cost $690.9 billion, and AI agents no longer wait. The page then summarises outside items. Acosta Group found 34% of shoppers use AI tools for shopping, led by ChatGPT and Google Gemini, with 25% routinely using Gemini for product searches. Gen Z and millennials drive adoption, using AI for comparisons, research and in store decisions, though only 22% trust agents to purchase autonomously. Albertsons Media Collective launched Retail Media Incrementality Based Multi Touch Attribution with LiveRamp, linking exposure data across owned channels, Meta, offsite media and third party inventory to Albertsons transaction data. Amazon Web Services launched Amazon Connect Talent, an agentic AI hiring platform. Crocs replaced scripted self service with Rivet, a Salesforce Agentforce powered conversational AI assistant.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: IHL Group says its 2026 study covers 96 specialty retail brands and finds inventory data accuracy, not AI budget size, separates winners from laggards. It says inventory distortion is down to $1.7 trillion, while empty shelves still cost $690.9 billion. Acosta Group found 34% of shoppers use AI tools for shopping, 25% routinely use Gemini for product searches, and only 22% trust agents to purchase autonomously. The page also states that most retail AI budgets fund the wrong layer first.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in retail can use this page as a dated signpost to IHL Group's argument that inventory data accuracy matters more than AI budget size, and that AI spending often targets the wrong layer first. It also offers quick, attributed examples of shopper AI use, retail media attribution, agentic hiring and conversational customer service. Because the page only summarises items, it is best used to identify reports or case studies to pursue, not to understand methods, sample details or measured outcomes.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Retail

sections.body: The page is a commercial landing page for IHL Group's research and advisory services, not a full research report. It gives headlines and short summaries, so it lacks methodology, definitions, sample construction and independent verification. Several items are about vendors and launches, including Albertsons, Amazon Web Services and Crocs, and the page does not state whether those summaries are sponsored or independent. The dated items run from 6 August 2026 to 10 September 2026, and the page was harvested on 29 September 2026, so it is a partial snapshot rather than a complete or current view of the retail AI field.
